subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add a delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and what public config shape should own that security boundary?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix adds public config surface and changes how security-sensitive tool-deny inheritance behaves between requester agents and subagents.

options.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
options.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy design
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/15032 defines a broader spawn-time capability model that also covers requester self-denial.

options.title: Reject new config surface
options.body: Document separate agent IDs or strict behavioral routing as the supported pattern, accepting that config-level separation of duties remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Sponsor delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add a documented selfDeny/delegateOnly-style field with deny precedence, /tools visibility, and tests for requester-hidden but child-inherited tools.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history for the current tool-policy implementation and recent maintainer routing points to steipete.
